newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Persson says concerned about weak EMU.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Persson says concerned about weak EMU.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Tuesday he would like to have a strong European economic and monetary union (EMU) and was concerned about the prospect of a weak EMU.
"We want to have a strong EMU," Persson told a news conference at the ruling Social Democrats party meeting.
"I am concerned it will be weak. I want people to stick firmly to the convergence criteria (of the Maastricht Treaty)."
Persson said the Swedish government had work to do, needing to lower government debt from current levels of about 76-77 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Under the Maastricht Treaty, state debt should be at or approaching 60 percent of GDP.
"We must drive down the debt/equity ratio of GDP to a situation where we are not so vulnerable," Persson said.
"I don't feel comfortable with a debt level of 60 percent of GDP."
